en.title: Minimum Flow Difference After Cutting One Edge of a Drainage Tree
en.description:
The tree is rooted at 0, and each node has a direct inflow. Cut exactly one parent-child edge to split the tree into two parts, minimizing the absolute difference between the two parts' total direct inflow.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and the solution; additions for bounds missing from the source and corrections to the examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains n values of parent, and the third line contains n direct inflows. Complete original bounds: 2≤n≤100000, inflow 1..10000, parent[0]=−1, 0≤parent[i]<i, and the tree depth is at most 500.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 0; 2; 9999. They have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Since every parent has a strictly smaller index, add each subtree's flow to its parent in decreasing order of index, then try every non-root node as the root of the cut-off subtree.
